captions.text: A founder starts with a deadline and scattered evidence — not a finished presentation.
Product requirements, measured results, research notes, and visual direction arrive together as evidence.
The founder chooses the working model and approves each external request before evidence leaves the workspace.
NodeSlide organizes the evidence into one six-slide investor argument, then compiles editable slides.
The story chooses the right visual form: diagram for mechanism, chart for evidence, and math for the north-star metric.
Feedback begins at the object that needs work: clarify one investor takeaway without rebuilding the deck.
Before anything changes, the founder compares a validated candidate and decides whether it earns approval.
Current research strengthens one claim, with separate web consent and a source bound to the result.
One editorial direction can align two chosen slides while every slide outside that set stays untouched.
They clarify the source-bound prototype chart while every uploaded numeric value remains unchanged.
The north-star metric stays inspectable as a formula, not baked into pixels.
Visual polish remains structured too, so the founder can rebalance a slide without losing editability.
A rights-cleared visual carries its alt text and credit into the same reviewed story.
At any point, the founder can see what the agent read, changed, validated, and sourced.
Long-running work remembers only the scoped editorial preference the founder deliberately saves.
The reviewed deck is immediately ready for the meeting and for frozen sharing.
The team keeps control after handoff: editable PowerPoint plus validated, inspectable deck JSON.
